'''Bernhard Nikolaus Philipp Pattenhausen''' (July 7, 1855 – August 25, 1926) was a German [[geodesy|geodesist]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Society |first1=American Mathematical |title=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |date=1926 |publisher=Society |page=726 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Bulletin_of_the_American_Mathematical_So/-obxAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=bernhard+pattenhausen&pg=PA726&printsec=frontcover |access-date=26 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He co-founded the [[Lohrmann Observatory]] in [[Dresden]] in 1913.<ref>{{cite web |title=History of the Lohrmann Observatory |url=https://tu-dresden.de/bu/umwelt/geo/ipg/astro/observatorium/geschichte?set_language=en |website=TU Dresden |access-date=26 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Pattenhausen was born in [[Darmstadt]], Germany in 1855, the twelfth child of a family of merchants. He studied engineering at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] from 1872 to 1876.

==Career==
After graduating from KIT, Pattenhausen worked for two years as an assistant to [[Wilhelm Jordan (geodesist)|Wilhelm Jordan]]. He received a post-doctoral habilitation in 1889 which enabled him to teach independently at a university. He also worked at the Ducal Forestry Institute in [[Braunschweig]] for several years before being appointed director in 1893. That year, he was made professor of [[mathematics]] and geodesy at the [[TU Dresden|Dresden University of Technology]], becoming [[Rector (academia)|rector]] in 1907 or 1908.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Education |first1=United States Bureau of |title=Report of the Commissioner of Education Made to the Secretary of the Interior for the Year ... with Accompanying Papers |date=1908 |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |page=322 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Report_of_the_Commissioner_of_Education/E8Qwz_nv1IMC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=bernhard+pattenhausen&pg=PA322&printsec=frontcover |access-date=26 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

Pattenhausen was director of the Mathematical and Physical Salon in[Dresden after 1894. He was appointed chairman of the Society for Geography in Dresden from 1904 to 1919, and became a [[privy council|Privy Councillor]] in 1906. He co-founded the [[Lohrmann Observatory]] at TU Dresden in 1913.<ref>{{cite web |title=UNESCO Portal to the Heritage of Astronomy - Show entity |url=https://web.astronomicalheritage.net/show-entity?identity=230&idsubentity=1 |website=web.astronomicalheritage.net |access-date=26 November 2025}}</ref>

He was awarded an [[honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from the [[TU Braunschweig|Braunschweig University of Technology]] in 1926. He died of a stroke in 1926 and was burined in the Tolkweitz cemetery of Dresden.
